title: Quantifying Uncertainty in AI Visibility: A Statistical Framework for Generative Search Measurement
abstract: arXiv:2603.08924v3 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: AI-powered answer engines are inherently non-deterministic: identical queries submitted at different times can produce different responses and cite different sources. Despite this stochastic behavior, current approaches to measuring domain visibility in generative search typically rely on single-run point estimates of citation share and prevalence, implicitly treating them as fixed values. This paper argues that citation visibility metrics should be treated as sample estimators of an underlying response distribution rather than fixed values. We conduct an empirical study of citation variability across three generative search platforms--Perplexity Search, OpenAI SearchGPT, and Google Gemini--using repeated sampling across three consumer product topics. translated_title: 量化AI可见性中的不确定性：生成式搜索测量的统计框架
translated_abstract: arXiv:2603.08924v3 公告类型：替换交叉 摘要：AI驱动的答案引擎本质上是非确定性的：在不同时间提交的相同查询可能产生不同的响应并引用不同的来源。尽管存在这种随机行为，当前测量生成式搜索中领域可见性的方法通常依赖于单次运行的点估计，如引用份额和普及率，隐含地将它们视为固定值。本文认为，引用可见性指标应被视为底层响应分布的样本估计量，而非固定值。我们对三个生成式搜索平台——Perplexity Search、OpenAI SearchGPT和Google Gemini——进行了引用变异性的实证研究，使用三个消费产品主题的重复采样。采用了两种采样方案：九天内的每日收集和十分钟间隔的高频采样。我们表明，引用分布遵循幂律分布。
tldr: 本文提出将生成式搜索中的引用可见性指标视为样本估计量，并通过跨平台和多种采样频率的实证研究，揭示了引用分布遵循幂律规律，从而为量化AI搜索中的不确定性提供了统计框架。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes treating citation visibility metrics in generative search as sample estimators, and through empirical studies across platforms and sampling frequencies, reveals that citation distributions follow a power-law, providing a statistical framework for quantifying uncertainty in AI search.
